analysis: This PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (changed head lines 808-823, a new paragraph on segmented paged admission) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (three new env-var rows at head lines 1687-1689). No executable code changed, so no new controls were removed. I examined the supplied head text for inference.md around lines 1235-1793 (unchanged context) and the CLI patch. The documented behavior describes parking free 64 MiB KV segments per pool, capped at min(2 GiB, slot grant/8) outside the grant/ledger charge, and wrapping zero-fill-on-demand host pages so new segments avoid device zero-fill. It also adds env toggles DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. Relevant threat IDs are T-028 (residual KV data in GPU memory after request completion) and T-041/TB-007 (cache and timing). Remaining integration questions for a later pass, which cannot be verified from the docs: (1) whether reinstalling parked, previously used segments to a different request/tenant is zeroed or fully overwritten before reads, given T-028's residual-data concern; the doc says only new segments use zero-fill-on-demand pages, and the reuse path's zeroing is not stated. (2) Whether parked backing, held outside the ledger charge, can cause memory-accounting gaps and availability issues; the doc says it is dropped on refusal, memory pressure and 30 s idle. (3) The allocator-cache sweep and reuse timing could add a small timing side channel, but this is speculative and no source was supplied. The actual implementation files (EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, PagedKVGroup.swift, GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift) were not supplied, so no finding is raised. The description of env knobs only as rollback toggles (=0 restores previous behavior) does not widen the attack surface.
